items.title: Device-scoped fleet status, maintenance, and reboot control
items.summary: Track Maven, Forge, Pi-hole, and optional read-only appliances through persistent status cards while restricting maintenance and reboot authority to explicitly supported devices.
items.implementation: The Guided Maintenance dashboard loads a private atomic fleet snapshot, renders one card per device, and exposes Maintenance and Reboot only on supported mutable cards. The Operations Topology view reads one bounded local /proc/net/route projection and renders the primary network path as WAN/provider cloud → detected default gateway → detected local subnet → known devices; management, containment, DNS, provider, inventory, and planned backup relationships remain supplemental below it. A reviewed enrolled gateway supplies its identity and status, while an unmatched route produces an inert evidence-only node. Forge and Pi-hole operations use fixed SSH aliases, fixed shell-free command vectors, fresh digest-bound previews, exact device confirmations, one global identity-checked lock, redacted receipts, and no automatic mutation retry. Reboot sends one request, requires a changed boot identity and fixed device-specific readiness, then replaces the snapshot. An optional Cisco 8851/Webex Calling card performs one bounded reachability probe, asserts no registration or firmware state, and has no mutation controls. Deployment addresses live only in ignored environment configuration. A status-only systemd timer collects at noon and midnight.
items.technologies: Ruby bounded services and typed application operations; OpenSSH fixed aliases; bounded ICMP appliance probes; APT and Pi-hole fixed vectors; Proxmox VE and LXC; JSON snapshots and receipts; SHA-256 digest binding; systemd user oneshot/timer; vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS Dashboard.
items.interfaces: Administration → Guided Maintenance; Collect fleet status; status-only appliance cards; supported per-device Maintenance and Reboot dialogs; evidence-driven Operations Topology network map; persisted status cards.

Every mutation completed with a terminal receipt; the hardened Forge reboot withheld snapshot replacement until Proxmox, LXC, Pi-hole service, version, DNS, and blocking readiness all passed.

items.title: Portable Linux fleet discovery and capability enrollment
items.summary: Generalize Guided Maintenance from the Operator's reviewed fixed devices into an explicit subnet-discovery, review, and enrollment flow for supported Linux and appliance targets.
items.implementation: A1 accepts one human-selected private IPv4 subnet, performs one 30-second-bounded nmap discovery pass after an explicit click, and retains candidates only in the page session. Configured, enrolled, and ignored identities are excluded from actionable candidates. One bounded local ARP-table read and Nmap's OUI data add ephemeral MAC, vendor, interface, and neighbor-state hints. Only the last successful canonical subnet is remembered. Digest-reviewed enrollment writes one owner-private 0600 record; ignored candidates have a separate reversible private list. Status-only enrollment may be fixed or DHCP-tracked by one reviewed MAC/subnet; SSH inventory remains fixed and requires an existing literal alias whose HostName equals the selected address. A2 adds one bounded per-device Refresh and Checked timestamp. A3 verifies a tracked current-IP MAC, performs one bounded recovery scan on mismatch or absence, retargets only one exact status-only MAC match with bounded address history, and permits one transient ten-minute retry before backing off. Compact status-only cards show IP, assigned name, Online/Offline status, Refresh, checked time, probe, and reachability. Fleet states use green for Healthy/Online, yellow for Updates available, and red for Offline/Reboot required.
items.technologies: Ruby bounded command runner and typed discovery/status services; nmap host discovery and OUI database; Linux /proc IPv4 ARP evidence; fixed BatchMode OpenSSH inventory; IPAddr subnet validation; SHA-256 preview binding; atomic owner-private JSON; one hardened transient systemd-run user oneshot; capability vocabulary for pacman, yay, paru, apt/apt-get, dnf/dnf5, zypper, apk, Flatpak, Snap, and Nix; Dashboard JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and existing application envelope.
items.interfaces: Administration → Guided Maintenance → Discover & enroll a device; explicit subnet scan; candidate Review or Ignore; status-only fixed/DHCP or fixed SSH inventory enrollment; reversible ignored list; private registry removal; compact status-only and rich managed cards; per-device Refresh and Checked evidence; Makefile checks and deterministic verifiers.
